chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Hamza ibn Humran, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

I asked him about a man who emancipated half of his slave girl, then accused her of adultery. He said: 'I view upon him fifty lashes, and he should seek forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for his deed.' I said, 'What is your view if she frees him from his accusation of her and forgives him?' He said: 'There is no whipping upon him if she forgives him before she raises the case (to the judge).'

key_terms.أَعْتَقَ نِصْفَ جَارِيَتِهِ: Emancipated half of his slave girl

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd penalty for accusing a partially freed slave girl of adultery, and does her forgiveness affect it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the specific application of the hadd penalty for slander (qadhf) within the context of manumission, where the Imam prescribes fifty lashes and seeking forgiveness. It highlights the Shia legal principle that the victim's voluntary forgiveness (‘afw) before the case is formally elevated to the judge waives the corporal punishment, emphasizing the restorative nature of justice in these cases. This ruling underscores the interplay between fixed divine penalties and the rights of the individual to forgive.
